title: Rainy city packing
content: For rainy urban trips, prioritize a compact umbrella, waterproof jacket, water-resistant shoes, quick-dry socks, and a zip bag for electronics. Choose layers rather than bulky outerwear.

title: Hot sunny destination packing
content: For sunny warm destinations, pack sunglasses, sunscreen, breathable clothing, swimwear, sandals, a reusable water bottle, and a hat. Plan outdoor activities early or late to avoid peak heat.

title: Cold weather packing
content: For cold trips, pack thermal layers, warm socks, gloves, a scarf, a hat, moisturizer, and shoes with good traction. Layering helps adjust between outdoor cold and indoor heating.

title: Museum and food itinerary
content: For travellers who enjoy museums and food, combine one major museum per day with neighbourhood exploration, a local market, and a relaxed dinner reservation. Avoid overloading the schedule.

title: Nature and hiking itinerary
content: For nature-focused trips, check weather before hikes, start early, bring water and snacks, and keep a backup indoor activity in case of rain or storms.

title: Public transit travel tips
content: When using public transit, group activities by neighbourhood, check last train or bus times, and keep the itinerary flexible. Pick accommodation near a central station.

title: Walking travel tips
content: Walking-based itineraries work best when stops are close together. Include breaks, comfortable shoes, and a backup ride option for bad weather or fatigue.

title: Rainy day itinerary
content: On rainy days, prioritize indoor markets, galleries, museums, cafes, cooking classes, bookstores, and scenic transit rides. Save parks and viewpoints for clearer weather.

title: Beach itinerary
content: For beach trips, include morning beach time, shaded lunch breaks, sunscreen reapplication, hydration, and a dry change of clothes. Watch wind and UV conditions.

title: Family-friendly pacing
content: A comfortable itinerary usually has one anchor activity per morning, one lighter afternoon activity, and flexible evenings. Leave buffer time for transportation and meals.
